title: Topological Persistence
notes: Open by positioning persistence as a scale-aware extension of homology. Homology tells us which components, loops, and voids exist at one scale; persistence asks when those classes appear, how long they remain visible, and which disappear as the filtration grows. Keep the chapter source span visible so students understand the lecture is a reconstruction of Chapter VII, pages 149 through 174.

title: Scale, Noise, Feature
notes: Use this slide to separate the philosophical motivation from the calculation. Noise is not a theorem-level category, so the chapter offers measurements rather than a universal decision rule. The key promise is that a long interval in a diagram is evidence for a feature at the chosen scale, while short intervals mark candidates for scale-dependent noise.

title: Elder Rule
notes: Read the merge tree from bottom to top. Components can merge but they do not split in a sublevel filtration of a connected space. At a merge, the component born earlier keeps its identity and the younger component receives a death time. This convention is what makes component counts over every interval match the path decomposition.

title: Filtration From A Function
notes: This is the first formal contract. A function on simplices can drive a filtration only when it is monotone on face inclusions; otherwise a higher-dimensional simplex might arrive before its boundary and the sublevel set would fail to be a complex. The threshold lab asset uses the triangle order to make that monotonicity inspectable.

title: Homology Through The Filtration
notes: Shift attention from spaces to vector spaces connected by inclusion-induced maps. Birth means a class is not inherited from the previous stage. Death means its image first becomes explained by an older class or by a boundary in a later stage. This is the Elder Rule translated from components to homology classes.

title: Persistence Diagram Read-Off
notes: Make the diagram do computational work. A point records a birth value and a death value, and vertical distance from the diagonal is persistence. To recover a persistent Betti number, count points born no later than the left threshold and dying after the right threshold. Emphasize the closed vertical and open horizontal convention.

title: Matrix Reduction
notes: Present matrix reduction as a single algebraic sweep that recovers all finite persistence pairs. Columns are reduced from left to right over F2 until no two nonzero columns share the same lowest one. A zero reduced column signals birth; a nonzero reduced column with lowest row i pairs that birth simplex with the current death simplex.

title: Triangle Worked Example
notes: Walk through the triangle slowly because it is the audit example for the whole algorithm. The dummy reduced chain element accounts for reduced homology, vertices two and three birth components, edge six births a loop, and the face kills that loop. The listed pivot pairs should be read directly as diagram points.

title: Sparse Implementation
notes: The sparse version stores only active columns as sorted lists, so the picture changes from a dense matrix to migrating linked lists. Every collision cancels the current top simplex and moves the list leftward. This monotone movement is the source of the output-sensitive runtime estimates based on nested birth-death intervals.

title: Zeroth Persistence Via Union-Find
notes: Dimension zero deserves a separate mental model. Vertices always create components, and an edge either joins two different components or closes a graph cycle. Union-find names each component by its oldest vertex, so the Elder Rule is built into the data structure. The JSON check confirms that the union-find pairs match the reduction pairs.

title: PL Surface Filtration
notes: For a piecewise linear height function on a triangulated surface, thresholds between vertex heights have the same homotopy type as lower-star subcomplexes. This is why a continuous surface problem can be fed to a finite simplicial algorithm. The important implementation detail is to add an entire lower star at the vertex value.

title: First Diagram From The Complement
notes: Explain the dimension-one shortcut by turning the surface upside down. A finite one-dimensional class of f corresponds to a component event for the complement, equivalently to a zero-dimensional event for negative f. Reflecting points across the minor diagonal converts the zero-dimensional diagram of negative f into the finite part of the one-dimensional diagram of f.

title: Extended Persistence
notes: Ordinary persistence leaves essential classes unpaired because they survive to the complete space. Extended persistence solves this by continuing with relative groups as the complementary superlevel set grows downward. The resulting sequence begins at zero and ends at zero, so every class receives a death event and every critical point can be paired.

title: Duality And Symmetry
notes: Use this slide as a theorem-level organizing view rather than a proof. Lefschetz duality relates absolute and relative homology in complementary dimensions, which becomes reflection across the main diagonal in diagrams. Comparing f with negative f introduces minor-diagonal and central reflections. The visual checks that ordinary, extended, and relative pieces move by the stated maps.

title: Lower/Upper Star Block Matrix
notes: Now connect the abstract extension to computation. Matrix A is the ascending lower-star pass. Matrix B is the descending upper-star pass. The permutation block P glues them by matching each simplex with its cone partner. After reduction, pivots in the three quadrants become ordinary, extended, and relative subdiagram points.

title: Spectral Sequence Summary
notes: Close by showing spectral sequences as another ordering of the same reduction information. Instead of sweeping columns strictly left to right, the algorithm reduces block diagonals phase by phase. After r phases, the total rank along a fixed dimension counts diagram points whose persistence is at least r, so the rank grid is a reorganized persistence summary.
